name: Methylphenidate
short: Blocks DAT and NET; acts only at the transporters.
mechanism: Blocks the **dopamine (DAT)** and **norepinephrine (NET)** transporters, enhancing synaptic dopamine and norepinephrine. Unlike amphetamine it targets **only the monoamine transporters**, much as SSRIs act at SERT.
uses: Indirect dopamine agonism also improves depression and wakefulness (Table 2-5)

facts.text: A “stimulant” for ADHD that acts on **DAT and NET**.
Targets **only the monoamine transporters** (not VMATs), in contrast to amphetamine.
Approved for sleepiness in **narcolepsy** (not OSA or shift work, used off-label); highly effective but controlled (abuse, diversion, psychosis, mania, hypertension).
Blocks NET and DAT **allosterically** (a site distinct from the monoamine site), like antidepressant reuptake inhibitors: stops the pump, is **not transported** and has **no VMAT2** action.
Racemic: the **D-isomer** is much more potent than L at both NET and DAT; single-enantiomer **dexmethylphenidate** also available.

Table 11-1 formulations: IR Ritalin/Methylin (3–4 h), Concerta (12 h), Ritalin LA (two peaks), Metadate CD, Aptensio XR, Quillivant XR, QuilliChew ER, Daytrana patch, Cotempla XR-ODT, **Jornay PM** (evening dose, delayed 10 h), Adhansia XR.
OROS, LA and transdermal forms are **slow-dose** stimulants (tonic signaling, lower abuse); IR is **pulsatile**.

updates.title: Stronger stimulant warnings
updates.text: In May 2023 the FDA required the boxed warning of all prescription stimulants to describe the risks of **misuse, abuse, addiction and overdose** consistently and to tell patients never to share them.

name: Dexmethylphenidate (D-methylphenidate)
short: The more potent D-enantiomer of methylphenidate.
mechanism: The single **D-enantiomer** of methylphenidate, much more potent than the L form at both **NET and DAT**; blocks them allosterically without VMAT2 action.

facts.text: Table 11-2: **Focalin** IR (early peak, 4–6 h; ages 6–17) and **Focalin XR** (peaks at 1.5 and 6.5 h, 8–10 h; ages 6–17 and adults).
XR D-methylphenidate is a **slow-dose** stimulant.

updates.title: A prodrug combination
updates.text: **Azstarys** (serdexmethylphenidate, a dexmethylphenidate prodrug, plus IR dexmethylphenidate) was approved on March 2, 2021 for ADHD from age 6.

name: Amphetamine
nbn: Dopamine and norepinephrine releaser (DAT/NET and VMAT2 substrate)
short: A transported substrate of DAT, NET and VMAT2: two targets.
mechanism: A **false substrate** carried into the neuron by **DAT and NET** (DAT has high affinity for amphetamines), and also a **transported substrate of VMAT2** in synaptic vesicles. Amphetamine therefore has **two targets**: the monoamine transporters and VMATs. Reuptake inhibition and release of dopamine stimulate D1–D5 receptors indirectly.

targets.note: Competitive inhibitor/substrate at high doses; displaces DA

uses: Indirect dopamine agonism improves depression and wakefulness (Table 2-5)

facts.text: Listed in Table 2-1 as a false substrate of both **NET and DAT**.
**Amphetamine has two targets**: monoamine transporters and VMATs (as a transported substrate).

Dopamine release by amphetamine causes a **paranoid psychosis** much like schizophrenia: a cornerstone of the dopamine hypothesis. Table 4-1 lists psychostimulants as **D2 agonist** models with auditory hallucinations, paranoid delusions and no insight.
A false substrate of **VMAT2** that competes with natural transmitters; dopamine or amphetamine are the “too hot” end of the Goldilocks analogy.
Amphetamine is also a **weak, reversible MAO inhibitor**; some MAOIs (tranylcypromine, selegiline via metabolites) are closely linked to amphetamine.
Approved for sleepiness in **narcolepsy** (not OSA or shift work, used off-label); highly effective but controlled (abuse, diversion, psychosis, mania, hypertension).

A **competitive inhibitor and pseudosubstrate** at NET and DAT. At ADHD doses the difference from methylphenidate is small; at abused doses it enters vesicles via VMAT2, displaces DA, opens channels and **reverses DAT**, causing euphoria.
**D-amphetamine**: D > L at DAT, so relatively more DAT action. **Mixed D,L salts**: D ≈ L at NET, so more NET action than D-amphetamine, but still DAT > NET.
Tables 11-3/11-4: Adderall and Evekeo IR (from age 3), Adderall XR, **Mydayis** (up to 16 h), Adzenys XR-ODT/ER, Dyanavel XR; D-amphetamine Zenzedi, ProCentra, Dexedrine spansule.
Spansules and XR mixed salts are **slow-dose**; IR forms are **pulsatile**, with more abuse potential.
Abused amphetamine (high dose, fast routes) blasts mesolimbic DATs; therapeutic doses boost tonic PFC dopamine.

updates.title: An amphetamine patch
updates.text: **Xelstrym** (dextroamphetamine transdermal system), worn 9 hours once daily, was approved on March 22, 2022 for ADHD in adults and children aged 6 and older.

updates.title: Stronger stimulant warnings
updates.text: In May 2023 the FDA required the boxed warning of all prescription stimulants to describe the risks of **misuse, abuse, addiction and overdose** consistently and to tell patients never to share them.

name: Lisdexamfetamine
nbn: Dopamine and norepinephrine releaser (DAT/NET and VMAT2 substrate)
short: Lysine-linked prodrug of D-amphetamine: a slow-dose stimulant.
mechanism: **D-amphetamine linked to lysine**: inactive until the lysine is cleaved, releasing D-amphetamine slowly for gradual, sustained transporter occupancy. (The book says cleavage occurs in the stomach; it actually occurs mainly in **red blood cells**.)

facts.text: Not absorbed as active drug until slowly converted to D-amphetamine plus L-lysine, so it rises **slowly rather than rapidly**.
Table 11-4: lasts up to **12 h**, peak 3.5 h, once in the morning.
A **slow-dose** stimulant: enhances tonic NE/DA with hypothetically lower abuse potential.
The **only approved** treatment for **binge eating disorder**, perhaps via striatal neuroplasticity rather than appetite suppression.

updates.title: Generic lisdexamfetamine
updates.text: The FDA approved the first **generic** versions of Vyvanse in late August 2023, amid ADHD stimulant shortages.

updates.title: Stronger stimulant warnings
updates.text: In May 2023 the FDA required the boxed warning of all prescription stimulants to describe the risks of **misuse, abuse, addiction and overdose** consistently and to tell patients never to share them.

name: Atomoxetine
short: Selective NET inhibitor approved for ADHD in children and adults; no abuse potential.
mechanism: A **selective NET inhibitor (NRI)**. Blocking prefrontal NET raises **both NE and DA** there (NET clears DA in the PFC); few NETs in the **nucleus accumbens** means no rise in DA there and **no abuse potential**. Continuous blockade restores tonic α2A/D1 signaling and dampens phasic NE/DA.
uses: **ADHD** in children and adults (the only well-studied, approved NRI)

facts.text: Raises prefrontal NE and DA but **not** accumbens DA: hence no reinforcing, abuse or addiction potential.
In stressed, comorbid ADHD, chronic use may restore tonic signaling, downregulate phasic NE/DA and desensitize receptors, possibly easing **anxiety, depression and heavy drinking**.

24-hour relief; smaller short-term effect sizes than stimulants, but not necessarily inferior in **stimulant-naïve** patients or after 8–11 weeks. High doses may cause **sedation or cognitive impairment** (α1): lower the dose.

name: Viloxazine ER
nbn: Norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor; serotonin receptor actions
short: NET inhibitor with 5HT2B/2C actions; a nonstimulant for ADHD.
mechanism: Inhibits the **norepinephrine transporter** and also acts at **5HT2B and 5HT2C** receptors. Once marketed abroad for depression but never in the US; repurposed as a controlled-release form for ADHD.

facts.text: A selective NRI in late-stage development for ADHD as a controlled-release formulation (Figure 11-45).

updates.title: Viloxazine approved
updates.text: **Qelbree** was approved on April 2, 2021 for ADHD in ages 6–17 and on April 29, 2022 for adults. Nonstimulant, not controlled; the label calls it a serotonin norepinephrine modulating agent and warns of suicidal thoughts and behaviors.

name: Reboxetine
short: Selective NRI listed among NET inhibitors used for ADHD.
mechanism: A **selective NET inhibitor**: like atomoxetine, raises NE and DA in the PFC but not in the nucleus accumbens.
uses: Listed among NET inhibitors used for ADHD with variable success (Figure 11-38); not approved for ADHD

facts.text: One of several NRI-acting drugs used for ADHD with varying success; only atomoxetine is well investigated and approved.

name: Guanfacine
short: α2A-selective agonist; ER form approved for ADHD alone or with stimulants.
mechanism: A **direct α2A agonist**, **15–60×** more selective for α2A than α2B/α2C. Stimulates postsynaptic α2A receptors on PFC pyramidal spines (Gi, ↓cAMP, HCN closed), **strengthening the signal**. No DA receptor action, hence no abuse potential.
uses: **ADHD** (ER form), alone or as **augmentation** of stimulants

facts.text: **10× weaker** than clonidine at sedation and lowering blood pressure, yet **25× more potent** at enhancing PFC function. ER form allows once-daily dosing with fewer peak-dose effects; only the ER form is approved for ADHD.
Best monotherapy candidates may have low prefrontal **NE** with normal DA; no predictor beyond an **empiric trial**.
Approved as an **augmenting agent** after inadequate stimulant response; may especially help **oppositional** symptoms (low VMPFC NE).

name: Mazindol
short: DAT inhibitor once approved for appetite suppression; tested in ADHD.
mechanism: A **DAT inhibitor**, formerly approved as an appetite suppressant.

facts.text: Listed as a future ADHD treatment in testing.

name: Centanafadine
nbn: Serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine reuptake inhibitor (SERT/NET/DAT)
mechanism: Inhibits the **serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine** transporters.

facts.text: A triple (5HT–NE–DA) reuptake inhibitor in testing for ADHD.

updates.title: Centanafadine approved
updates.text: **Simtriyo** was approved on July 24, 2026 for ADHD in adults and children aged 6 and older (once-daily ER capsule), after four positive phase 3 trials; launch awaited DEA scheduling.
